topics.title: CI vs CD
topics.description: A CI/CD pipeline automates building, testing, and deploying software so teams can deliver code changes more frequently and reliably.

definitions.description: Regularly merging code changes into a shared repository, followed by automated building and testing.
Automating the release process so that code can be reliably deployed to production at any time.
keyElements: Automated deployment to staging and testing environments
benefits: Ability to gather user feedback quickly

definitions.description: An extension of continuous delivery where every change that passes all stages of the production pipeline is deployed to production automatically, without human intervention.
keyElements: Continuous Delivery: changes are ready for production but require manual approval
Continuous Deployment: changes are automatically deployed to production

topics.title: Pipeline Stages
topics.description: The six stages a change passes through from commit to release.

stages.name: 1. Source
activities: Code is committed to a version control system such as Git or SVN
Code is pulled from the repository

stages.name: 2. Build
activities: Artifacts are generated: JAR, WAR, Docker images

stages.name: 3. Test
activities: End-to-end tests verify entire application flows
Performance and load tests evaluate system behavior under load

stages.name: 4. Deployment
activities: Artifacts are deployed to various environments
Infrastructure provisioning when using infrastructure as code

stages.name: 5. Validation
activities: Integration tests in the deployed environment

topics.title: Pipeline Design
topics.description: Design principles that keep a pipeline fast, repeatable, and trustworthy.

practices: Fail fast to provide immediate feedback
Pipelines should be repeatable with the same outcome
Avoid state dependencies between pipeline runs
Define pipelines in version-controlled configuration files
Treat pipeline configuration like application code
Follow the test pyramid: more unit tests, fewer end-to-end tests
Implement test automation at all levels

topics.title: Security

Use secret management tools integrated with CI/CD
complianceChecks: Enforce policy compliance as part of the pipeline

topics.title: Deployment Strategies
topics.description: How new versions reach production without taking it down.

howItWorks: Direct traffic from the old to the new version after validation
Easy rollback by switching traffic back
Release to a small percentage of users first
Gradually increase the percentage if successful
Deploy code to production but keep new features disabled
Enable features selectively for testing or gradual rollout

topics.title: Interview Questions
topics.description: The ten questions this topic is most often tested on.

questions.question: What is the difference between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment?
answer: CI: frequent integration of code changes with automated testing
CD: automating the release process for reliable production deployments
Continuous Deployment: automatically deploying every change to production

questions.question: Explain the stages of a typical CI/CD pipeline.
answer: Source, build, test, deployment, validation, and release stages

questions.question: What tools have you used for implementing CI/CD pipelines?
answer: Discuss experience with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and similar tools

questions.question: How do you handle database changes in a CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Tools like Liquibase or Flyway for versioned database migrations
Testing migration scripts in isolated environments
Rollback strategies for failed migrations

questions.question: Explain different deployment strategies and when to use them.
answer: Blue-green for quick rollbacks and zero downtime
Canary for gradual rollout with user feedback
Rolling updates for resource-constrained environments

questions.question: How do you secure secrets in a CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Secret management service integration
Environment variables for sensitive information
Avoiding hardcoded credentials

questions.question: How do you ensure the quality of your CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Monitoring pipeline metrics
Implementing comprehensive testing
Regular pipeline audits and improvements

questions.question: What are feature flags and how do they relate to CI/CD?
answer: Feature flags decouple deployment from feature release
They allow testing in production with limited exposure
They enable continuous deployment while controlling feature availability

questions.question: How do you handle dependencies between microservices in a CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Contract testing
Versioning APIs
Parallelizing independent service deployments

questions.question: How do you implement infrastructure as code in your CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Tools like Terraform, CloudFormation, or ARM templates
Version controlling infrastructure definitions
Testing infrastructure changes in isolated environments
